about: ep02 terrain/seafloor regions for HawaiiStage.loadRegion(root, name) (engine/www/lab/hawaii/hterrain.js). Heights: RG 16-bit PNG, h = v / 65535 * hrange + hmin, row 0 = north. stack = layers finest first, each inside the next. Facts are measured on the baked grid (not survey values): use them to stage shots, check every narrated number against the fact ledger.

bigisland.purpose: Big Island hero (also covers Maui Nui at lower detail): frame 1 / thumbnail NO OCEAN, s001-s003, s047-s070 drained massif, s150-s176 payoff and refill. Unchanged so frame 1 still matches final_ep02_1.jpg.
gaps: Seafloor is ETOPO 2022 15" (about 460 m) on a 120 m grid: flank gullies are procedural detail; the Kohala reef terraces are coarse (use kohala), Kamaʻehuakanaloa has no pit craters (use kamaehu, same limit).

The Hawaiian Deep (s057) is one water body at -5,000 m and three pools at -5,500 m (north of Molokaʻi and Maui, NE of the island, east of Hilo): pick the level from facts.grid.water_left_at, do not sculpt a ring.

facts.note: DEM summits are smoothed by the grid (Mauna Loa survey 4,169 m, Mauna Kea 4,207 m, Everest 8,849 m).

grid.saddles_note: highest sea level (m) at which the two points are joined by dry land on this grid (4-connected); null = not joined above -7,000 m

hawaii_skirt.purpose: ETOPO 30" context around the main islands; the outer layer of every main-island stack.

mauinui.purpose: s004-s013 Maui Nui -400 ft (-122 m) one island, the dry Au'au Channel, Penguin Bank, drain to -1,000 m and refill; s089 Maui (Haleakala); thumbnail arm B (final_ep02_2.jpg).
gaps: Seafloor ETOPO 2022 15" (about 460 m): the dry Auʻau Channel floor for the 1.5 km pass and the 40 m ground camera (s007-s008) is smooth; only procedural micro-relief adds texture there.
Saddles on this grid: Maui-Lānaʻi -59 m, Maui-Molokaʻi -80 m, Kahoʻolawe -159 m; at -122 m Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi are one island and Kahoʻolawe is separate (matches the script).

facts.saddles_note: highest sea level (m) at which the two points are joined by dry land on this grid (4-connected); null = not joined above -7,000 m

oahu_nuuanu.purpose: s025-s043 windward O'ahu, the Ko'olau pali, drain NE to -4,500 m, the Nu'uanu debris field and the largest block (summit about -2,691 m at 22.065N 157.072W), Manhattan drag; s090 O'ahu and Honolulu.
gaps: Offshore seafloor ETOPO 2022 15": the large Nuʻuanu blocks are resolved (largest top -2,712 m here vs -2,691 m in the script source), smaller blocks are not; the deposit outline and other slide footprints must be traced from USGS I-2809, they are not in the data.
NCEI 1/3" covers Oʻahu and its shelf to 22.06N / 157.45W only.

kauai.purpose: s080-s081 Kaua'i rim in the age sequence; s091 Kaua'i (label) before the Waimea Canyon drop; s092 the flight past Ni'ihau.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" topo-bathy covers both islands: no gap for the regional shots.

facts.saddles_note: highest sea level (m) at which the two points are joined by dry land on this grid (4-connected); null = not joined above -7,000 m

main_chain.purpose: s049-s050 the -4,000 m pullback (all main islands on one ridge), s057 the Hawaiian Deep strip left at about -5,500 m, s080-s082 the age pullback and the crash zoom out, s092 flight NW past Ni'ihau.
gaps: ETOPO 2022 15" on a 333 m grid; the 30" hawaii_skirt beyond it shows stair-stepped waterlines at deep levels, keep the horizon hazy.
All main islands are joined by dry land at -3,008 m (Kaʻieʻiewaho Channel, Oʻahu-Kauaʻi), so "one ridge by about -4,000 m" holds.

facts.saddles_note: highest sea level (m) at which the two points are joined by dry land on this grid (4-connected); null = not joined above -7,000 m

kilauea_sf.purpose: s014-s024 Kilauea's south flank and coast (the 1975 slide, whole coast moving), s044-s046 the creeping flank, s086-s088 the south coast at the end of Chain of Craters Road and the Holei sea arch site.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" (hilo_13) covers east of 155.47W and north of 19.17N; the Kaʻū side uses Terrarium z13, offshore south of 19.17N is ETOPO 15".
The Hōlei Sea Arch (collapsed Sept 2026) is below the grid and the DEM predates the collapse: model it, both states, from the dated NPS photos.

halape.purpose: s016-s023 Halape cove at a 1-3 km oblique (pre-dawn), the coastal block dropping about 3.5 m and the flooded grove.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" (2011) shows today's post-1975 shore: the pre-1975 ground for the 3.5 m drop must be rebuilt by raising the coastal block in the shot; palms, tents and the cove beach are not in the data; colour is HLS 30 m (soft at 1-3 km).

pali.purpose: s026-s031 the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout ground shot (about 1,200 ft, looking NE over windward O'ahu), the tourist and hat gag, the dive down the cliff; s090 callback.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" (USGS 10 m land): the lookout (343 m on this grid), its wall, the road and trees are not in the data; HLS 30 m colour is soft at ground level (needs a close-up texture or paper props).

waimea.purpose: s091 the camera drops into the red walls of Waimea Canyon under a rain squall.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" land (USGS 10 m): canyon walls resolved; HLS 30 m colour; rain squall and waterfalls are effects.

maunakea.purpose: s065 the summit access road gag on Mauna Kea's upper slope (never on Pu'uwekiu), s061 the Mauna Kea label.
gaps: Terrarium z14 (USGS 3DEP 10 m) plus hilo_13 in the east: the summit road is only a 30 m colour streak, no road geometry; telescopes not modelled (and not wanted).

kamaehu.purpose: s150-s158 Kama'ehuakanaloa (Lo'ihi), the young volcano about 30 km off Kilauea's coast, water drained to about -1,500 m, the COMING SOON sign on the summit platform.
gaps: Offshore it is ETOPO 2022 15" only (hilo_13 stops at 19.17N): the summit ridge stands out (top about -1,000 m) but the summit platform and pit craters (s151) are below the grid. Higher-resolution multibeam (SOEST HMRG) was not reachable (TLS error); until then any pit craters drawn are approximate and must be marked so.

kohala.purpose: s076-s079 the drowned coral-reef terraces off west Hawai'i (Kohala), low raking light on the drained flank.
gaps: NCEI 1/3" (kawaihae_13) covers north of 19.87N: check the drowned-reef terraces on the still before highlighting steps (s077: only where the bathymetry shows them).

nwhi_chain.purpose: Context layer for the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands flights (s092-s111, s140-s146): Ni'ihau to Kure on one grid, across the antimeridian.
gaps: ETOPO 2022 30" (about 0.9 km): the NW Hawaiian islets are removed from this context layer (sub-pixel and partly false in ETOPO); the close regions carry them.

nihoa.purpose: s093-s099 Nihoa fills the frame (sea cliffs, terraced valleys), then the pull wide over its big bank.
gaps: Land from Terrarium (SRTM): plan area right (0.6 km2, real 0.69) but the relief is smoothed: top 179 m vs 273 m surveyed, so the sea cliffs are too gentle. Terraces and house sites are not in the data. The bank is ETOPO 15" (false land removed).

lalo.purpose: s100-s108 Lalo (French Frigate Shoals): the lagoon, La Perouse Pinnacle (last tooth), East Island before and after 2018.
gaps: Worst gap: ETOPO 2022 15" has a 57 km2 false island over French Frigate Shoals and no reef or lagoon relief; after cleanup the atoll is a featureless shallow platform. La Pérouse Pinnacle (about 37 m) is below every grid (-11 m at its spot): model it at its surveyed position. East Island is a 6 m speck. Use sat.jpg (HLS 30 m, reef and lagoon visible) for the look; the July and October 2018 before and after must come from dated Landsat/HLS scenes, not baked here. A real fix is satellite-derived depth calibrated on the NCEI Midway survey.

gardner.purpose: s109 Puhahonu (Gardner Pinnacles): the last pair of basalt rocks poking out of open sea.
gaps: The two pinnacles (52 m) are a 13 m Terrarium speck at the right place: model the rocks at their surveyed position; bank from ETOPO 15" (false 859 m land removed).

nwhi_west.purpose: s123-s124 Midway regional, s133-s139 the carrier wreck sites more than 3 miles down (lines from the atoll), s140 flight to Kure, s144-s146 the Darwin Point line (about 29N) and the drowned seamounts NW of Kure (crosses the antimeridian).
gaps: ETOPO 2022 15": at the 1942 wreck positions the floor is -5,312 m (Yorktown), -5,317 m (Akagi), -5,439 m (Kaga), all more than 3 miles; the abyssal plain there is smooth interpolation, no abyssal hills (s138 needs procedural relief). Islets are removed (sub-pixel).

midway.purpose: s112-s122 Midway Atoll (reef ring, Sand Island, the albatross ground shot, drain and cut-away), s123 June 1942 hero shot, s137 drain around the atoll.
gaps: Best data in the set: NCEI 1/3" (2012) topo-bathy, referenced to mean high water, so the reef flat sits within about 1 m of level 0 and reads as foam: lower foam or level a little for clean water. HLS 30 m colour.

kure.purpose: s140-s143 Kure (Holaniku), the last atoll, its reef ring tinted blue, the cut-away where the reef barely keeps up.
gaps: ETOPO 2022 15" only: the reef ring and lagoon are not resolved (lagoon -2 m on the grid), Green Island 11 m from Terrarium (real about 6 m). Use sat.jpg for the reef ring; the cut-away (s143) is schematic.

everest_wide.purpose: Context layer for the Everest summit gag.
gaps: Terrarium z11 (SRTM): context only.

everest.purpose: s064 the paper climber on Everest's summit (real snow); the same-scale comparisons stay on BlockStage (lab/hawaii/data/everest_h16.png).
gaps: Terrarium z14 (SRTM 30 m): summit 8,748 m on the grid vs 8,849 m surveyed (the same-scale comparisons stay on BlockStage, which scales to 8,849 m). HLS 30 m, November 2023 snow.
